title: Prove exact repeated-st tariffs for independent monotone prices (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration, produced by Nick Petalas. For d repeated A2 targets st, independent nonnegative nondecreasing rank-price tables and separate finite caps have exact complete formal cost H_s(d)+H_t(d), where

```text
H_u(0) = 0
H_u(m) = min_{1 <= k <= min(b_u,d,m)} [tau_u(k) + H_u(m-k)]
```

This removes the common-price and concavity restrictions from ToikY's #6821. Its separate-letter rank demands are cited inputs. Each rank list can be reduced to exact demand using monotonicity; independent minimizing s and t partitions then attain the full group-algebra endpoint. The theorem holds over every field with arbitrary rank-capped scalar couplings, free scalar GL mixing and arbitrary finite restored dirty spectators.

The first example has d=7, cap four, tau_s(k)=3+k^2 for k>0 and tau_t(k)=k/(k+1). The s-ranks are (2,2,2,1), costing 25; the t-ranks are (4,3), costing 31/20. The exact bill is 531/20. Applying parts (4,3) to both letters costs 651/20, six more under this declared abstract tariff. This comparison evaluates a legal word; it does not apply the predecessor's concave formula outside its hypotheses.

Only research/a2-st-monotone-tariff/ is added. [Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19538484). The delivered scope matches the claim and permits separate caps explicitly.

Credit ToikY #6821 for the formal endpoint and selective-cut application; Adam Gall #1941 and Ross Richardson #1966/#1989 for separate-letter cuts; Benny Zhao / zhaobenny #6817 and David Arias #2738 for the retained framework; and the ywz65, eumemic, Ali Romman and Gareth Davidson register-model lineage. Classical partition dynamic programming and monotone clipping are not claimed as new methods. Nick Petalas's older #4846 is a related monotone-tariff precedent for the distinct UT3 central target. No predecessor scientific program was replayed.

## Evidence

Local CPython 3.12.15 on macOS arm64, standard library only, at head fc55af2406dd0be798d1a1fa241098f117fafa4a:

- 1,125 exact partition optima agree with an independent count-vector oracle, including 846 nonconcave cases and zero prices; 17,772 excess-rank truncation cases satisfy the new price bound.
- 212 complete signed formal endpoints over Q/F2/F3/F5 include 64 unequal-cap cases. All 1,180 paid couplings have their asserted ranks; 424 couple an arbitrary dirty role through scalar gauges with both boundary maps included.
- A separate faithful regular-action implementation checks 1,344 full basis columns. All 1,180 paid-call omissions, 212 missing scalar boundary maps and seven invalid optimizer inputs reject.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized direct commands print PASS_A2_ST_MONOTONE_TARIFF and compare the entire freshly generated source-hash receipt. Each took 1.44 seconds in a single local timeout check. The registered runner executed both commands and printed PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE in 3.12 seconds. These are timeout observations, not a performance comparison.
- Metadata, exact source pins, committed bytes, modes and source-history ancestry pass. The official seven-file export passes integrity checks and normal/optimized Git-free direct replays. No local mathematical check is deferred solely to CI.

Reproduce from the repository root; another installation may substitute its own CPython 3.12 executable:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/a2-st-monotone-tariff
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/a2-st-monotone-tariff/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/a2-st-monotone-tariff/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/a2-st-monotone-tariff --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Direct replay writes no files and imports no predecessor code. RESULT.json is generated by --emit-receipt, never handwritten. Universal coverage comes from PROOF.md using the cited rank-demand premise; finite checks are corroboration rather than enumeration of all circuits.

## Limitations

This is a formal tariff, not a native implementation, supplier admission, new kappa or multiplication theorem. Scalar coupling rank is not an admitted recursive child rank. Native realization, scalar-map costs, frames, movement, ownership, storage, stock, precision, all-size compilation and the complete supplier/consumer invoice remain unknown. All five selected framework assumptions remain. The selected frontier and frozen sources are unchanged. Decreasing prices, changed targets and additional paid/free address labels are outside the theorem. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed; Lean, Docker, the selected cold replay and predecessor scientific suites were not run.

## Open next questions

- Can an actual native rank-capped call support a complete nonconcave or letter-dependent price table that benefits from independent partitions? First specify its arbitrary-input entry/exit boundary and charge every physical and recursive obligation. No such native call or rank conversion is supplied here.
- For one explicitly decreasing price table, can a complete dirty-restored word beat the exact-mass partition relaxation, or can an exact replacement be proved? Monotone truncation no longer applies. No continuation is reserved.

## Related open work

- [#7179](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7179) studies five longest-element A2 targets with rank cap three and a common concave price. This contribution treats repeated st with independent monotone tables and computes no common numerical optimum.
- [#3893](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3893) studies the mixed three-role S3 endpoint diag([s],[t],[st]) with rank-one unit-priced calls. The endpoint and tariff differ; no common numerical optimum is computed here.
